behavioral_effects: A conversation's second and later turns expose previously discovered MCP tools on the first model request instead of re-paying a search_tools round-trip (one extra model call) per turn
Discovered-tool state is sticky per conversation: refreshed when discovered or called, aged out after 3 unused turns, capped at 24 tools LRU-first, LRU-capped at 16 conversations per socket
compatibility_impact: None. build_mcp_toolsets and build_toolsets_for_user gained an optional keyword-only 'discoveries' parameter (default None keeps prior behaviour for channel traffic and direct callers). The replayed exchange uses the same ToolSearchCallPart/ToolSearchReturnPart shape pydantic-ai's ToolSearch capability already emits, appended after the rebuilt history so the OpenRouter prompt-cache prefix of prior turns is unchanged.
limitations: Discovery folded from a cancelled turn covers only tools actually called before the stop; discovered-but-uncalled tools from a cancelled run are re-searched next turn
State is per WebSocket session: a reconnect or second tab starts with an empty discovery log until tools are used again
Native-path discoveries (NativeToolSearchReturnPart) are read but untested against a live native-tool-search provider; this deployment uses the local search_tools path via OpenRouter
reason: Discovered MCP tool state lives only in ToolSearchCall/ToolSearchReturn parts of the in-memory pydantic-ai message history, but agent_session rebuilds history from Postgres as plain text each turn, so every turn that needs an MCP tool re-pays a search_tools round-trip (one extra model call); tracking discovered names per conversation and replaying them as a synthetic tool-search exchange makes discovery sticky without destabilizing the OpenRouter prompt-cache prefix
risks: Replayed-but-unused tool schemas cost input tokens until their TTL expires (bounded at 24 tools)
A server dying within MCP_PROBE_TTL_SECS can have names replayed until the cached probe verdict expires — same staleness window the toolset attachment itself already had
rollback: git revert of the single commit. No schema, config, or persisted-data changes; the discovery state is in-memory per WebSocket session and disappears on restart, so nothing outlives the code.
security_impact: Reviewed via security-review pass: no new findings. Replay serializes only MCP tool names already model-visible via search_tools, validated against the set attached this turn (probe + read-only assertion + allowlist), so a disconnected server's names cannot reach the model. State is per-WebSocket, keyed by ownership-checked conversation ids — no cross-user or cross-conversation path. The three standing MCP findings (approval-gating asymmetry, no connection-time SSRF revalidation, URL-embedded credentials unencrypted) are neither narrowed nor widened: revealing a schema removes a search round-trip, not an approval control, and approval-gated Google toolsets do not participate in discovery replay.
summary: Persist MCP tool discovery across chat turns via conversation-scoped replay in the agent session
